figures.claim: 2. Figure 2: Trade-off between KL divergence and path adherence for different guidance methods and strengths. Points closer to the origin represent better overall performance. Error bars represent standard deviation over 5 runs.
figures.explanation: Execution stage: The trade-off scatter plot (Figure 2) does exist and correctly shows KL divergence vs path adherence for different guidance methods. However, the paper claims 'Error bars represent standard deviation over 5 runs' — this is fabricated: (1) plot.py uses ax.scatter() with no xerr/yerr parameters, (2) no 5-run replications exist anywhere in the repository, (3) no standard deviation data exists in any final_info.json. The visual claim of error bars cannot be generated from the code and is absent from both the original and freshly reproduced figure.
figures.evidence: plot.py lines 116-128 use ax.scatter() with no error bar parameters; no plt.errorbar() calls; final_info.json files contain only 'means' keys, no 'stds'; only single runs exist (run_1 through run_4), no 5 replications; freshly generated kl_path_tradeoff.png and original repo kl_path_tradeoff.png both show scatter points without error bars. | Code: plot.py:120 (ax.scatter without error bars); plot.py:119 (only 'means' accessed, no 'stds')
